name: adv_qat_bad
title: Quantization-aware training and TorchScript export - nine planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_advanced_clean/qat_export.py, hardening round 2, 2026-09-14
note: The QAT lifecycle - prepare_qat, train, calibrate, convert, trace, save - has three defects that are specific to it and that no rule models: observers calibrated on the TEST loader, `convert()` run on a module still in train mode, and a TorchScript trace taken before `eval()`, which bakes the 0.4 dropout mask into the exported graph. MLView finds eight of the rest, and correctly identifies `calibrate()` as an evaluation region over held-out data even though the function is not named like one.

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the parameter initialisation, the dropout mask and therefore the observed activation ranges all move between runs, so two quantized exports of the same code differ

expected.defect: the device names cuda outright with no availability check
expected.why: fbgemm QAT is a CPU-targeted configuration, so this file cannot run at all on the machine it is quantizing for

expected.defect: the training loader is built with shuffle=False and no sampler
expected.why: CIFAR-10 is class-ordered on disk, so each batch is nearly single-class and the BatchNorm statistics the fake-quantization observers watch are wrong

expected.defect: num_workers=4 with no `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard anywhere in the module - main() is called at module scope on the last line
expected.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2 (finding DGRG-20, re-reported as the MLV112 half of the round-2 sweep): `r_data._import_time_chain` now follows the module-scope call chain transitively instead of one hop, so `print(main())` -> `fit()` -> `build_loaders()` is seen for what it is. Original note: MLV112's `_runs_at_import` follows exactly one hop; `build_loaders()` is called by `main()`, which is called at module scope. See finding DGRG-20.

expected.defect: calibrate() runs the model without model.eval()
expected.why: the 0.4 dropout is active and the BatchNorm running statistics keep updating, so the observers record the ranges of a randomly-thinned network rather than of the network that will be exported

expected.defect: calibrate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built for twenty calibration batches that are never differentiated

expected.defect: the batch loop never calls optimizer.zero_grad()
expected.why: every step applies the sum of every batch's gradients, which with fake-quantization noise on top diverges quickly

expected.defect: the float checkpoint pickles the whole module instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the module moves

expected.defect: torch.load passes neither weights_only= nor map_location=
expected.why: an untrusted checkpoint executes arbitrary code on load, and a CUDA-saved file fails outright on a CPU-only machine

forbidden.why: the test loader is built with shuffle=False at line 53
the order in the batch loop is backward (76) then step (77)
there is no torch.no_grad() anywhere in this file
train_epoch accumulates loss.item() at line 78, never the tensor
QuantisableNet.forward returns the dequantized Linear output; nothing softmaxes before CrossEntropyLoss
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
QuantisableNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line
quant, dequant, features, dropout and head are plain attributes, which nn.Module registers
there is no split call; CIFAR10(train=True) and CIFAR10(train=False) are two separate downloads

unsupported.defect: the observers are calibrated on the TEST loader, so the quantization ranges are chosen from the held-out distribution
unsupported.why: calibration is a fit on data, but not through an sklearn transformer, so MLV101/MLV102 do not reach it.

unsupported.defect: convert() runs on a module still in train mode, so the fake-quantization parameters are frozen from training-time BatchNorm statistics
unsupported.why: no rule models the QAT lifecycle's eval-before-convert requirement.

unsupported.defect: the TorchScript trace is taken before eval(), so the 0.4 dropout mask drawn at trace time is baked into the exported graph
unsupported.why: no rule models tracing a module in train mode; it is the single most common export bug and it is silent at run time.
